chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who rented a house in which there was a garden, and he planted in the garden, and planted date-palms, trees, fruits, and other things, and he did not seek the permission of the owner of the house concerning that.

He said: He is liable for the rent, and the owner of the house assesses that planting and crop, then gives it to the planter if he had sought his permission concerning that. But if he had not sought his permission, then the rent is upon him, and the planting and crop belong to him; he may uproot it and take it wherever he wishes.

key_terms.الْكِرَى: rent due for the leased property
key_terms.بُسْتَانٌ: a garden or orchard attached to the property
key_terms.غَرَسَ: planted trees or set growth into the ground

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a tenant plants trees or crops in rented property without the landlord's permission?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a tenant who plants crops and trees in a rented property. If he planted with the owner's permission, the owner may assess and compensate him for the planting; if he planted without permission, he still owes the rent, while the planting remains his property and he may remove it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3896 - Muhammad bin Muslim narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Al-Baqir (as)

regarding a man who rented a house that included a garden.
The tenant planted crops, palm trees, and other fruit-bearing trees without seeking the landlord's permission.

Imam (as) said: "He is responsible for paying the rent.
The landlord should evaluate the plants and crops, and compensate the tenant if he had sought permission for planting them. However, if the tenant did not seek permission, he is still responsible for paying the rent, but the plants and crops belong to him. He may uproot them and take them wherever he wishes."
